W5 (contrarian), after E028. Every forecast now starts from the tip, E027: 8.75 epochs, 219 steps, 20/24/28/32 px at 0/15/40/70% of steps, 5.878 s, 0.7547.
1. Time model correction. I overpredicted time in 6 of the last 7 runs. The run is GPU-bound and costs about 23 ms per step on average. Converting an early 24 px step to 20 px saves about 5 ms (E026: −0.18 s for 34 steps).
2. New mechanism, from E028's surprise. Truncating the backward pass through group 1 and the whitening layer for the last 25% of steps saved 0.84 s. That is about 13%, against a 4–5% FLOP estimate. So backward work near the stem is far more expensive than its multiply-add share. It is memory-bound: GELU/BN backward plus input-gradient work on 31×31 maps with 24/128 channels. Accuracy fell only about 0.2 pp, so the trade is about 4 s per pp, much better than the epoch dial (about 1.2 s per pp). Hidden lever nobody has proposed: in the code, the whitening bias is "frozen" after step 75 only by setting its LR to 0. It still has requires_grad=True, so every step still computes the input gradient of group-1 conv1 and the whitening GELU backward at full resolution, then throws it away. Setting requires_grad=False after step 75 (a second captured graph variant) should save about 2–4% of time with bit-identical maths. A gentler FreezeOut variant may also give most of E028's saving for under 0.1 pp: freeze only the whitening path plus group-1 conv1 in the last 15% of steps.
3. Resolution. Early low-resolution steps are nearly free (E026). Late low resolution, or a big jump into the 32 px tail, costs 0.3–0.9 pp (E011, E018, E024). The stem-mismatch story is still unproven. The whitening is followed by GELU and BN, so a per-resolution whitening fix probably matters little.
4. Hyperparameter plateau. Weight decay, label smoothing, Muon lr and the averaging ramp all land within ±0.2 pp of each other (E013, E014, E016, E022, E025). Muon in the code has no weight decay, so E016's change acted only on the SGD groups (H1.5.4 is effectively true). Averaging knobs are flat.
5. Noise. A rebuild moves the 3-seed mean by about 0.05 pp. Any change to step count or RNG is a fresh draw, with a 3-seed SD of about 0.25 pp. The tip's true mean is about 0.7545, so the margin over 0.753 is thin.
6. Epoch dial. Each −0.25 epoch saves about −0.14 s and costs about −0.12 pp.
Unsure: whether the wasted whitening-bias backward really costs 2–4%; how results transfer to the PCIe judge; whether held-out seeds confirm the tip.

forecasts.reason: It is effectively a 9% step cut, like the epoch dial; selecting on high loss under LS 0.3 won't recover the lost accuracy.
Averaging knobs are flat; a +0.15 pp held-out gain is unlikely.
Underfitting regime; dropping smoothing late sharpens logits but unsettles the averaged weights; net about zero or negative.
33 more steps at 20 px instead of 24 px save about 0.15 s; the early low-res phase is nearly free per E026; same RNG draw.
GELU+BN after whitening absorbs most of the mismatch; small extra prepare cost; the effect is within noise.

cruxes: Does setting whiten.bias.requires_grad=False after step 75 (a second captured graph variant; the LR is already 0 there) cut 2–4% of time with bit-identical accuracy? Today the backward still computes and discards the group-1 conv1 input gradient and the whitening GELU backward at full resolution on every step.
Does a gentler FreezeOut (truncating only the whitening layer and group-1 conv1, last 15% of steps) keep most of E028's 13% saving for under 0.1 pp held-out loss?
Is the tip's held-out seeds 3–12 mean really at least 0.7535, or is the 0.7547 on seeds 0–2 a lucky draw that leaves no margin to spend?
